text:
ana: experiment idea — I'm prototyping a new traffic generator mode to stress the runtime in a way that matches our worst tails. goal: produce controlled long-tail + microburst interplay so we can benchmark kernel selection and batching heuristics apples-to-apples. thoughts?

matt: love it. what's different from existing 'burst' profiles?

ana: the key is correlated bursts + prefix locality. we want spikes that reuse kv-cache prefixes 60-80% of the time but still inject cold keys to exercise kv-warmup. also variable QPS ramps (sine -> step -> staircase) so kernel selection gets real sequence-length and batch-shape variance.

devin: +1. need deterministic seeds and workload replay support. without deterministic seeds we can't compare kernel A vs B. include rng_seed and a fingerprint output.

ana: yup. plan is to output a compact "seed manifest" per run that has timestamps + request hashes so replays are bit-identical. also adding an option to replay real traffic traces but overlay our ramping.

sara: for apples-to-apples we should freeze runtime flags (no auto-fallback) and run each kernel variant as a separate job with identical batcher settings. also record GPU power/SM utilization. otherwise noise kills p99 diffs.

matt: batching knobs to expose? max_batch_size, batch_timeout_ms, eager_pack_threshold, grouping_window_ms — plus a knob for preferring homogeneous sequence-length packs vs mixed.

leo: add metrics: qps, p50/p95/p99/p99.9, tail-latency-curve, tokens/sec, kv_hit_rate, avg_batch_size, kernel_choice_counts, batch_wait_ms distribution, and gpu_util, mem_bw.

benchbot: perf job queued: job/loom/seed=42/profile=longtail/variant=A -> link: https://ci.internal/loom/1234 :white_check_mark:

ana: sample config (proto):
```json
{
  "profile": "loom-longtail",
  "qps_ramp": [ { "from": 50, "to": 1200, "over_s": 30 }, { "from": 1200, "to": 600, "over_s": 120 } ],
  "burst_pattern": { "type": "compound", "microburst_pct": 0.25, "spike_interval_s": 7 },
  "kv_warmup": { "locality_pct": 0.7, "cold_inject_pct": 0.3, "prefix_pool": 5000 },
  "seed": 42,
  "replay_overlay": "trace-2024-04-02-17",
  "batching": { "max_batch_size": 64, "batch_timeout_ms": 8, "eager_pack_threshold": 0.6 },
  "kernel_control": { "force_kernel": null, "allow_autotune": false }
}
```

sara: nice. add a switch to pin attention kernel variant and quant path so we can compare quantized vs fp. keep model version pinned.

devin: test harness note — add a "warmup-only" pass that runs initial N seconds with same QPS profile but no sampling of latency; that's for KV warmup and persistent cache stabilization. then do the measured pass. otherwise first-pass artifacts pollute results.

matt: for analysis we'll run pairwise diff plots for p95/p99 and plot batch-size vs latency scatter. also compute effective tokens/sec per GPU for cost comparisons.

leo: small thought — include an option to inject 'slow tail' requests (e.g., long context, heavy decoding tokens) at 0.5% to force different kernel paths. helps expose kernel selection regressions.

ana: agreed. will add slow_tail_inject_pct and a micro-config for those requests. implementation plan: extend existing generator with new profile + seed manifest + replay overlay + warmup pass + pinned-run mode. target PR by EOD Fri.

benchbot: queued job results: variant=A vs variant=B (same seed) — p99.9 delta: +18ms, avg_batch_size A=9.3 B=7.8, kv_hit_rate ~0.72. attaching logs to job/loom/1234. :eyes:

devin: that p99.9 looks actionable. can you re-run with warmup=120s and batch_timeout=6ms? also attach kernel_choice_counts.

ana: will re-run. assigning follow-ups: @matt draft analysis notebook, @devin add kernel counts to harness output, @leo add slow-tail injection config. I'll open a short RFC doc later today. :rocket:
